question: Which of the following causes of malabsorption occurs with alteration of the intestinal mucosa ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Celiac disease" -> "immune response to gluten" -> "damage to intestinal mucosa" -> "malabsorption of nutrients" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Achalasia" -> "esophageal motility disorder" -> "difficulty swallowing" -> "not primarily affecting intestinal mucosa" -> "unclear" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Cholestasis" -> "bile flow obstruction" -> "impaired fat absorption" -> "not directly altering intestinal mucosa" -> "unclear" -> 65%
CHAIN: "Crigler-Najjar syndrome" -> "disorder of bilirubin metabolism" -> "not related to intestinal mucosa" -> "no alteration of intestinal mucosa" -> " -> 0%
analysis: Celiac disease is an autoimmune disorder that leads to damage of the intestinal mucosa when gluten is ingested, resulting in malabsorption. The other options do not primarily involve alteration of the intestinal mucosa as their main mechanism of malabsorption.
